content.text: I reviewed the full package — brief, conversation (USER passages only as authority), disclosure, all ten draft sections, the numeral table, and all six figure briefs — and built a complete source ledger before concluding.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced; no unsupported or inconsistent matter found, so findings is empty. Coverage: (1) All 20 claims. Every limitation of claims 1, 11 and 16 traces to the disclosure — rigid base with first/second side, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side ("An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base"); rigid low-friction perimeter member terminating in a bearing face ("The perimeter of the second side is formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials"); clearance along at least part with continuous ambient inflow and sub-atmospheric chamber ("not intended to form a complete airtight seal ... restricts airflow into the chamber ... continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter, maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere"); all-rigid path with no elastomeric/foam/resilient member ("the vibration motor is connected to the tile through rigid components"); slidability under maintained differential ("the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact"). Dependents 2-9, 12-15, 17-20 each trace (closed loop/skirt; plastic, metal, PTFE, combinations; free of rubber/foam with rigid contact; holding without operator downward force; continuous running; vacuum pump; guiding handle; rope, wire, cable pulling element with decoupled control). Claim 10's stirring elements trace to the affirmative USER passage "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion", which also supports the autonomous clause in the Field and the FIG. 6 embodiment; the operational "resume/rebuild/publish" messages were treated as non-disclosure. (2) All 17 numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) each carry one meaning across the table, description and every brief, each appears on at least one sheet, and every numeral on a sheet is defined and used in the description. (3) All six figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings agree part-for-part, including the repaired FIG. 2 enumeration (slab/legs/band sectioned, extraction housing in elevation, motor and handle omitted) against the FIG. 2 brief's cut bodies. Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 use the same designation in the FIG. 3 source view (numeral 2 and 4 at each end, arrows perpendicular to each line), in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 brief view lines, and in section 07 and the detailed description; the horizontal line cuts the ring on both sides, consistent with FIG. 2's two legs, and FIG. 4 is fragmentary at one cut. Hatching is consistent for the same part across sheets (perimeter member rising to the right in FIG. 2 and FIG. 4; covering element falling to the right in both). (4) Depiction conventions stay inside the briefs: rectangular plan form, ring width, band depth, block order, port gap width/position/form, and stirring-element number/form/position are each disclaimed within the brief, while the application text and claims remain shape-neutral. Section 07 uses only "shown schematically" and "omitted for clarity" and contains no "by way of example", "any closed outline", or other embodiment-broadening justification of a renderer's choice. The functional surfaces were checked specifically: the bearing face is drawn only as the disclosed distal end face, and no untraced statement of taper, angle, runout, relative depth, radial or circumferential end position, or contact topology appears; the FIG. 2 gap asserts only the disclosed fluid communication from the extraction mechanism through the base to the chamber, and FIG. 4's clearance is the disclosed air path beneath the rigid perimeter, marked "shown enlarged for clarity". (5) No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in any of sections 01-10; the earlier FIG. 6 self-contradicting disclaimer is gone. Background prior-art characterizations (DE-202021002652-U1, US-11408462-B2, US-10001245-B2, US-4934475-A, US-11247858-B2) were not required to trace to the inventor and are left for the citation review; title, "Not applicable." cross-reference and government-support statements match the filing brief, and no means-plus-function language is present.

content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs against the disclosure and the affirmative USER passages in the conversation.

Key traces I verified:

- **Independent claims 1/11/16** — rigid base with first/second sides, motor on the first side, air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter member terminating in a bearing face, non-sealing clearance admitting ambient air, extraction rate sufficient to hold the chamber sub-atmospheric, all-rigid vibration path, and sliding under a maintained differential — all trace to the disclosure's fourth through sixth paragraphs ("rigid loop or skirt", "not intended to form a complete airtight seal", "continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter", "connected to the tile through rigid components", "slide freely across different areas of the tile").
- **Dependents** — closed loop (2), plastic/metal/PTFE/combination (3, 13, 20), free of rubber/elastomer/foam (4, 14), no operator downforce (5, 14, 19), continuous extraction (6, 15), vacuum pump (7, 15), handle (8, 19), rope/wire/cable pulling element (9, 12, 18), simultaneous hold-and-slide (17) — each has an exact disclosure sentence.
- **Claim 10 and the third embodiment** — traced solely to the affirmative USER turn beginning "field of the disclosure: ... we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion". The Field's "moving autonomously" and the FIG. 6 material rest on that same passage, not on the operational "resume/rebuild" turns, which I treated as non-disclosure.
- **Numerals 10–48** — each denotes one part, each appears in at least one brief, and every brief's name matches the ledger.
- **Figure conventions** — the rectangular plan form, band depth, block order, section-line angular position, cord attachment point and stirring-element count are disclaimed inside the briefs only; the application text and Brief Description stay shape-neutral and contain no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening. The FIG. 2 fluid-communication gap verbalizes only the disclosed first-side-to-chamber communication, with no taper, angle, depth-comparison or contact-topology statement.
- **Section designations** — 2-2 and 4-4 carry the same designation in FIG. 3's brief, the two sectional briefs, the Brief Description, and the detailed description; hatching directions agree across FIGS. 2 and 4.
- No drafting note, placeholder, open question, or instruction to a person remains in any application section.

No untraced or inconsistent matter found.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of independent claims 1 (device), 11 (system) and 16 (method) and of dependent claims 2-10, 12-15 and 17-20 was matched to an exact affirmative disclosure sentence: the rigid base with first and second sides, the vibration motor coupled to the first side, the air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, the rigid low-friction perimeter loop/skirt of plastic, metal, PTFE or a combination of rigid materials, the deliberate absence of a complete airtight seal, the clearance through which ambient air enters beneath the rigid perimeter, the continuous extraction maintaining the chamber below atmospheric pressure, the resulting differential holding the device without operator downforce, the all-rigid low-damping transmission path, free sliding to successive areas, the guiding handle, and the rope/wire/cable flexible pulling element with decoupled control. Claim 10 and the third (autonomous) embodiment trace only to the one affirmative USER turn beginning "field of the disclosure: ... we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"; the "resume", "rebuild", "revalidate" and "tighten" turns were treated as operational and not as disclosure, and the drafting agent's own YOU passages were excluded as support. All seventeen numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked: each denotes exactly one part, each name matches the ledger in every brief, and each appears in at least one figure; the non-consecutive run from 26 to 34 is permissible and creates no conflict. All six figure briefs were compared line by line with the Brief Description of the Drawings and the detailed description: FIG. 1 (10, 12, 18, 20, 24, 36, 44), FIG. 2 (12, 14, 20, 22, 24, 36), FIG. 3 (16, 24), FIG. 4 (24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42), FIG. 5 (10, 24, 36, 46) and FIG. 6 (10, 48) agree with their drawing descriptions, including the repaired FIG. 2 enumeration showing base, chamber, perimeter member and covering element in section with the air-extraction mechanism in elevation and the motor and handle omitted. Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 carry the same designation in the FIG. 3 brief, in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 briefs, in the Brief Description and in the detailed description, and the contact-at-2-2 versus clearance-at-4-4 assignment is covered by the disclosed "along at least part" limitation. Cross-sheet hatching directions for the perimeter member and covering element in FIGS. 2 and 4 are consistent. Depiction conventions (rectangular slab and plan form, band depth, three-block order, ring width, section-line angular position, cord attachment place, two stirring-element blocks) are declared schematic and confined to the briefs; they verbalize no taper, angle, deeper-end, runout or contact-topology relationship, and the FIG. 2 fluid-communication gap expresses only the disclosed first-side-to-chamber communication with port, duct and valve construction expressly not asserted. The application text and Brief Description remain shape-neutral, contain no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening added to justify a renderer's choice, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any section. Terminology (covering element, exposed face, bonding material, substrate, perimeter member, bearing face, clearance, air-extraction mechanism, low-friction material) is used identically in the claims, summary, description, abstract and briefs; claim antecedents resolve; the abstract is a single paragraph of about 142 words; and title, cross-reference and government-support sections match the filing brief. Background prior-art characterizations were left for the separate citation review as instructed. No unsupported technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency was found, so the findings array is empty.
